name: Semiconductor fab
bpBasis: The 2 BP #72 gives for a chip fab, from the design sketch, whose two semiconductor fabs this building follows: 2.5 t of electronic silicon a month at 60 MW, or 1.2 t of radiation-hardened ICs a month at 80 MW

name: Solar cell fab

real.plant: Mission Solar Energy cell fab, San Antonio, Texas (OCI)
real.basis: Mission Solar is adding a 2 GW a year solar cell fab with 500 long-term manufacturing jobs (pv magazine USA, 2025), 4,400 t of cells at the 2.2 g of silicon a watt Fraunhofer ISE gives for 2022; its power and water are not published

bpBasis: Mission Solar is investing $265 million in its 2 GW cell fab in Texas (pv magazine USA, 2025)

name: Battery plant

real.plant: Panasonic Energy Kansas Factory, De Soto, Kansas (Panasonic)
real.basis: Panasonic's Kansas factory is to make about 32 GWh of 2170 cells a year with up to 4,000 direct jobs (Panasonic, 2025), 132 kt of cells at the 243 Wh a kg of the Panasonic NCR18650B cell; Evergy supplies it with 110 to 170 MW (Flatland KC), the top of the range taken; its water is not published

bpBasis: Panasonic is investing $4 billion in its De Soto battery plant (Kansas Department of Commerce, 2025)

name: Magnet works

real.plant: NPM Narva sintered magnet plant, Narva, Estonia (Neo Performance Materials)
real.basis: Narva opened with an initial capacity of 2,000 t of magnets a year (Magnetics Magazine, 2025) and 100 employees making test batches (ERR, 2025); its power and water are not published

bpBasis: Neo Performance Materials' Narva magnet plant cost $75 million (Magnetics Magazine, 2025)

name: Data centre
bpBasis: The 1.8 BP #72 gives for a 120 MW data centre, the size of this one, $15M a MW; the Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide gives $17.6M a MW all-in for a greenfield site in the United States and Canada, excluding chips and GPUs
